notes.title: It’s your last chance to play Bioshock, Borderlands, and Stray via PlayStation Plus
notes.content:
While we already know that the likes of Far Cry 6, Inscription, and more will be arriving on PlayStation Plus in due course, PS Plus subscribers will be bidding farewell to some stellar games during July. Meaning that unless you cough up some cash or find a different service to play them via, now is your last chance to give these games a go.

The games leaving PS Plus can be found under the ‘Last chance to play’ collection on the PlayStation Store, and if they leave as the new batch of games arrives, they’ll likely be going on July 18. The games to be removed from PS Plus are as follows:

  • Stray
  • Saints Row: Gat Out of Hell
  • Marvel’s Avengers
  • Fluster Cluck
  • Raiden V: Director’s Cut
  • Rogue Stormers
  • Bioshock Remastered
  • Bioshock 2 Remastered
  • Bioshock Infinite: The Complete Collection
  • Borderlands: The Handsome Collection

notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30373242/c8895ec1c55f25385df94d3ade68936c2e95092c.jpg[/img]

For the players who have the setup issue on Xbox 360 or Xbox One controller, please read the article on this [url=https://www.howtogeek.com/234427/how-to-remap-buttons-on-your-steam-controller/]link[/url]. 

[UPDATE]
For Keyboard Users:
To switch the control from keyboard to controller, press START on the controller. 
To switch the control from controller to keyboard, exit to the main screen and press a key on your keyboard.
To start the co-op mode, press START on the controller when you select the fighters. 


Thanks for your feedback and patience! You can visit our  [url=https://www.ufointeractivegames.com/contact-us]contact us[/url] page to give us feedback directly.

notes.title: Raiden V brings my favourite pink bendy lasers to PC
notes.content:
It’s been a long time coming. First released as an Xbox One exclusive last year, veteran Japanese shmup studio MOSS have been released from whatever contractual obligation that bound them, and have now brought the latest, biggest and boldest game in the 25-year-old Raiden series to multiple systems – including PC – in the form of Raiden V: Director’s Cut [official site].
